newsitem.title: GREECE: Greek rates ease after cbank move, ecu/drs up.
newsitem.headline: Greek rates ease after cbank move, ecu/drs up.

text.p: Greek interbank depos and forex forwards eased after the central bank's move to boost liquidity via its 14-day fixed rate depo tender, dealers said.
Bonds were steady with an upward bias ahead of Thursday's auction and the drachma was weaker against the ecu, trading around its intraday high of 309.55, dealers said.
Trading activity in the forex market picked up without affecting the highly visible ecu/drachma rate which was trapped in the 309.10/25 band, traders said.
"Depos and forex forwards eased after the central bank chose to leave 50 billion drachmas in the system," said a senior dealer at a foreign bank. "The easing is more visible in short tenors."

The central bank drained 100 billion drachmas of 14-day funds at 11.90 percent today. A pact of about 150 billion drachmas was maturing today so that a net amount of 50 billion drachmas boosted the system's liquidity.

"Coupon bonds and FRNs are stable with a slight upward bias in late dealings," said a senior dealer at a private bank. "Bank of Greece sent a message to the market that prices were too low on Wednesday but the size of the intervention was small."
The central bank bought about 1.0 billion drachmas of seven-year FRNs due 2004 on Wednesday.
The dealer said market sentiment had been adversely affected by what seemed to be a temporary halt to the bond market's momentum on the upside.
"Foreign players show some interest for Thursday's auction," he said.
Greece will auction 150 billion drachmas of seven-year FRNs on June 26. The first coupon is set at 10.40 percent.
The mark was quoted at 157.91/01 from Wednesday's 157.900 fix, the dollar at 271.96/06 drachmas from 271.880 and the ecu at 309.46/56 from 309.350 drachmas.
"The ecu has gained ground against the drachma in late trade trading around the intraday high of 309.50/55," said a dealer at a foreign bank. "The trading range for the day is 309.0/55."
